Furthermore, We summarize the application of AI-assisted imaging technologies in the static characterization and dynamic monitoring of biofilms. We also consider the challenges associated with such integration and discuss approaches to overcome technical and methodological barriers. Additionally, we outline the prospects for AI-assisted biofilm characterization through interdisciplinary collaboration and innovation. Overall, the convergence of AI and advanced imaging technologies is poised to accelerate and further redefine the landscape of biofilm research. The future of biofilm research promises transformative breakthroughs in understanding microbial communities and their impact on health, environment, and biotechnology.

title: A closed-loop active learning method for investigating bubble breakup flow in pore-throat microchannels
abstract: Bubbly flow in porous media is a fundamental concern for versatile industrial processes. Microfluidics offers a promising approach to mimic pore-throat structures using locally constricted microchannels, enabling in-situ visualization of bubbles within micron- or millimeter-scale flow paths. In this research, a closed-loop workflow empowered by machine learning (ML) is proposed to efficiently investigate bubbly flow characteristics and extract scientific insights from data. The workflow integrates a convolutional neural network for image processing and bubble size quantification, random forest models associated with ensemble variance sampling for bubble behavior prediction and data-efficient guidance for experiments, and model explanation techniques to elucidate the underlying bubble breakup mechanisms. The uncertainty-driven data sampling strategy significantly reduces the experimental efforts required for model development. With only 116 experimental points being performed, the established ML models accurately predict the occurrence of bubble breakup, exhibiting strong interpolation and extrapolation abilities even under unseen experimental conditions. In addition to discovering the rules of bubble breakup, inverse optimization is exemplified to prepare target bubble swarms in the pore-throat microchannels using established ML models.

title: Integrated design, scale-up, and surrogate-based optimization of PSA systems for hydrogen purification from ammonia decomposition
abstract: Green hydrogen production from liquid organic hydrogen carriers such as ammonia is a key pathway toward decarbonization and net-zero emissions. However, hydrogen derived via ammonia decomposition must be further purified to meet stringent requirements of some applications, including adoption in fuel cells. This study presents a framework for the design, modeling, and multi-objective optimization of a purification unit based on pressure swing adsorption (PSA). An adsorption model was developed and validated against experimental isotherms and breakthrough data. The validated model was then scaled to industrial conditions to serve as a base-case simulation. A detailed sensitivity analysis was conducted to evaluate the impact of key operational and design variables—including bed length, diameter, pressure, temperature, and flow rate—on four critical performance indicators: hydrogen purity, recovery, productivity, and specific energy consumption (SEC). A surrogate model was trained using high-fidelity simulation data and integrated with the Non-dominated Sorting Genetic Algorithm II (NSGA-II) to generate Pareto-optimal solutions. The surrogate model's predictions were successfully validated against full-order simulations. The optimization results revealed three distinct operating regions, each representing a trade-off between purity, recovery, and energy efficiency. Notably, the proposed design achieves up to 99.99 % hydrogen purity with a recovery of 77.4 %, and SEC values as low as 5.19 MJ/kg H₂. Compared to baseline configurations, the recommended design achieves improvements of 2.78 % in hydrogen purity and 11.11 % in energy efficiency, offering a promising and scalable strategy for ammonia-based hydrogen purification systems. The economic assessment, based on technical performance, estimated the projected cost of purifying hydrogen to 99.99 % concentration using an industrial-scale PSA unit fed by ammonia decomposition.
